  unet+segformer ×3; a stall watchdog that dumps /proc/<pid>/task/*/{stack,wchan} of the container when the benchmark

  * unet nsys_3 detail: the two callbacks that never returned are the NITROS subscription callbacks of /r2b/image_rgb
    (sub 0x5D194255E630, thread 807) and /r2b/tensor (sub 0x77C3B0249990, thread 808, i.e. the TensorRT node input),
    both entered within 0.6 ms of each other at +161.298 s (07:00:37 UTC, during search probe 1, whose mean fps halved
    to 261 because the pipeline died mid-window). Two NITROS callbacks blocking each other = deadlock signature.
  * unet nsys_2 detail: during the 5 s fixed-rate playback (+308..+313 s) the ROS-level callbacks of the first stages
    (/r2b/image and /r2b/camera_info subs plus two downstream NITROS callbacks) ran at 9–10/s, i.e. the entry of the
    pipeline consumed the 10 fps playback, while the monitor saw nothing. NITROS hops inside a container are GXF-internal
    (no ROS callback), so a stall inside the GXF/TensorRT codelets is invisible to LTTng and leaves upstream ROS callbacks
    running. Unified reading of all three stalls: the GXF/CUDA part of the graph stops under nsys; when its input queues
    fill, the NITROS ROS callbacks block on the push (unet nsys_3 signature), otherwise they keep running (nsys_2,
    segformer nsys_3 signature). The ROS executor and services stay alive throughout, which is why the benchmark
    controller gets answers but zero messages. FISH/LTTng is not involved (base/lttng 0/75 stalls).

## Autoware lean run 2026-09-06 16:00 (overhead_aw_20260906_155912) — auto-stop self-kill, root cause found
- lttng #1: replay ended +152 s, the new run script waited 720 s for the trace-stop marker — it never came. Inside the
  container: `trace_session.sh stop` (the daemon's auto-stop child) was a ZOMBIE, /tmp/fish_session_dir.stopping still
  held, the daemon gone, LTTng session still running. Mechanism (deterministic): gpu.py auto-stop runs the stop script
  with subprocess.run(); the script's step 2 `fish.cli gpu daemon stop` SIGTERMs the daemon; the daemon's handler calls
  sys.exit() → SystemExit inside subprocess.run() → run() KILLS its child (the stop script) before `lttng stop` and
  before the RETURN trap that removes the lock. Every later stop (SIGTERM trap) then waits 900 s on the stale lock and
  returns without stopping the trace. This is also why this morning's lttng #1 (092416) was lost, and why yesterday's
  traced runs took 480–630 s to shut down (they only survived because the outer timeout was not reached... the trace
  was stopped by the wrapper's fallback path).
  Rescue: manual `lttng stop/destroy` inside the container + lock removal → 221 MB trace kept, run rc=0.
- Fix (python/fish/gpu.py + scripts/install_fish.sh): the daemon passes FISH_STOP_FROM_DAEMON=1 and the stop script
  skips the daemon-stop step in that case; the stop lock now records the owner PID and a waiter takes over when the
  owner is dead. Landed 16:18:45 — 5 s AFTER the nsys #1 container copied the scripts, so nsys #1 runs with the old
  code; a one-off rescue (scratchpad aw_nsys_rescue.sh) stops the LTTng session after the nsys exports and releases
  the lock. Every later container gets the fix.

## Model findings while building the DAG gallery (2026-09-06 19:00, session fish_20260906_151532 = AW lean nsys_1)
- gantt_spans are materialised lazily by the viz server (/gantt route); gpu_dag_pg needs them for callback anchoring.
  Without them every CUDA row is "out of span" and the whole GPU activity becomes thread-anchored (20 tid anchors,
  0 cb anchors). Fixed for this session by calling fish_viz_server._ensure_gantt_spans() first (1.39 M spans, 6 GPU
  submitter callbacks); gpu_dag_pg then gives 6 cb anchors and 0 tid anchors. TODO: make gpu_dag_pg build the spans
  itself (or make the model pipeline do it).
- Phase classifier bias: lidar_centerpoint's real steady shape (206 nodes: 125 CPU / 70 SM / 11 CE, 218 of 232
  invocations) is labelled UNKNOWN and a marginal 8-node shape (×10) gets STEADY, because per-frame cudaMalloc calls
  raise the init score above the STEADY threshold. Any node that allocates every frame will be misclassified; the
  scheduling statistics "over STEADY periods only" are then computed on the wrong shape. Gallery now picks the most
  frequent non-INIT shape as dominant; the classifier itself is unchanged (needs a malloc-tolerant rule).
- wcc_dag_viz.py builds FISH tasks over ALL comm edges: /clock, /parameter_events and /diagnostics glue the whole
  application into one 525-vertex "task". The FT definition (data edges only, infra excluded) must be applied there.
